If you are interested, I added a function to return padded JSON. I needed it for a project I'm working on and it seemed like the easiest thing to do was add the six lines of code into Flask.

Thanks for the awesome framework.

Tom

Conversation comments: captured 14 of 14 (1 page(s), per_page 100, body cap 4000 chars per item); complete for this endpoint.

--- comment 1: mitsuhiko (2010-09-01) [id 382640]
That does look interesting, but where is callback coming from? Also, it would need unittests and an import in the **init** file.

--- comment 2: ghost (2010-09-01) [id 383274]
The import in the init file is there. The callback is generated on the client side, so whatever function wants to generate the JSONP would have to get it from the client and provide it to the jsonify function. I can add a usage example when I get home from work.

I'll look through your unit tests and write one for this function.

Thanks for taking a look.

--- comment 3: galvez (2010-12-17) [id 618181]
+1 on this. Would play well with jQuery's getJSON() function (which uses JSONP if you add a "?callback=?" to the end of the URL (you can guess how this works... :))

--- comment 4: ghost (2010-12-18) [id 620332]
I'll try to get on writing some unit tests.

--- comment 5: subtlepath (2011-01-04) [id 650978]
JSONP should be returned with MIME type 'text/javascript', not 'application/json'.

--- comment 6: y3i12 (2011-04-24) [id 1050643]
Ok, it works and it would be an amazing feature to work with jQuery.
Just found a little error on return generation:
content = str(request.args['callback']) + '(' + json.dumps(dict(_args, *_kwargs)) + ')'
